name: High Middle Ages 1200
description: Christendom, the Islamic world, and the steppe on the eve of the Mongol storm. (Map borders approximate medieval realms onto modern outlines.)

FRA.name: Kingdom of France
FRA.note: Philip II Augustus is breaking Angevin power and centralizing the realm.

GBR.name: Kingdom of England
GBR.note: King John holds England and shrinking continental lands; the barons grow restless.

DEU.name: Holy Roman Empire
DEU.note: A contested crown over hundreds of princes, torn between Welf and Hohenstaufen.

ESP.name: Crown of Castile
ESP.note: Leading the Reconquista against the Almohads.

TUR.name: Byzantine Empire
TUR.note: Weakened and wealthy; Latin crusaders and Turks circle the old empire.

EGY.name: Ayyubid Sultanate
EGY.note: Saladin's heirs hold Egypt and Syria against crusader remnants and each other.

MNG.name: Mongol Khanates
MNG.note: Temüjin is uniting the steppe tribes. The world does not yet know his name.

ITA.name: Papal States
ITA.note: Innocent III wields excommunication and crusade as instruments of policy.

world.simulationRules: Medieval logic: dynastic marriages, papal authority, feudal levies, sieges, plagues, and slow communications. No nation-states — legitimacy flows from crowns, faith, and lineage. Travel and campaigning are seasonal and slow. Borders are approximations of realms, not modern states.
